title: Microsoft Purview DLP: restrict access to Fabric semantic models and lakehouses
summary: The briefing passes: its opt-in default, licensing, rollout dates and documented limitations are supported. Minor corrections should restore omitted wizard headings and explain the narrower capacity wording in the PowerShell reference.

claims.claim: The roadmap change adds a DLP restrict access action for Fabric semantic models and lakehouses.
claims.quote: DLP restrict access action allows you to block access to guest users or all users depending on what labels or sensitive information types matches your semantic models or lakehouses.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The action can block guests or all users based on matching sensitivity labels or sensitive information types.
claims.quote: DLP restrict access action allows you to block access to guest users or all users depending on what labels or sensitive information types matches your semantic models or lakehouses.

claims.claim: Audit and Policy Tip actions for sensitive content in these items were already supported.
claims.quote: This is in addition to the ability already supported by DLP policies to audit and notify users via Policy Tips based on sensitive content within Fabric semantic models and lakehouses.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.

claims.quote: "previewDate": "April CY2024"

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified on 11 November 2026 at 00:53:22.
The Learn overview describes restricting access to data owners or organisation members, with other users losing access.
claims.quote: the policy restricts access to the data owners or to members of the organization, depending on the policy configuration. All other users lose access to the item.

claims.claim: The troubleshooting page describes the all-users case as blocking everyone except workspace admins.
claims.quote: All users in the tenant: When applied to this group, DLP policies block all users except workspace admins, who can troubleshoot and fix the data, where relevant.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: UserType = Member is treated as internal even when the user signs in with an external account.
claims.quote: a member of the organization means a user with UserType = Member. This includes users who sign in with an external account. Because their UserType is Member, they’re treated as internal users.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Block only people outside your organization applies to UserType = Guest users.
claims.quote: users with UserType = Guest are considered external. The Block only people outside your organization setting applies to these Guest users.

claims.claim: The Learn overview still labels restrict access as preview.
claims.quote: Restrict access (preview). When you configure a policy with the restrict access action and a policy match occurs

claims.quote: | September 2026 | **DLP restrict access (Generally Available)** |

claims.claim: MC937920 was last updated on 26 March 2026.
claims.quote: Updated March 26, 2026: We have updated the timeline below.

claims.claim: MC937920 says semantic-model restrict access has been in public preview since November 2024.
claims.quote: DLP restrict access for sematic models is already available in Public Preview as of November 2024.

claims.claim: MC937920 gives mid-April 2025 as the beginning of lakehouse restrict access public preview rollout.
claims.quote: For Fabric lakehouse, public preview of restrict access will begin rollout mid-April 2025

claims.claim: MC937920 expected lakehouse public preview rollout to finish in late April 2025.
claims.quote: is expected to complete by late April 2025.

claims.claim: MC937920 gives late October 2026 as the start of general availability rollout.
claims.quote: General Availability: We will begin rolling out late October 2026 (previously June)

claims.quote: expect to complete by late November 2026 (previously end of June).

claims.claim: MC937920 sets no act-by date.
claims.quote: Act by: none

claims.claim: MC937920 singles out organisations with guests who should not accidentally access sensitive information.
claims.quote: This action is especially valuable when your organization has guest users, and you want to enforce proper restrictions to ensure these users do not accidentally access sensitive information.

claims.claim: Microsoft says rollout is automatic and requires no admin action before rollout.
claims.quote: This rollout will happen automatically by the specified date with no admin action required before the rollout.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: A security or compliance admin must create or update Fabric DLP policies to include the new action to start using it.
claims.quote: your security or compliance admin will need to update or create new DLP policies for Fabric to include the new Restrict access action.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The new control is admin-opt-in: it applies no new restriction until an admin adds it to a policy.
claims.quote: If your organization does not wish to start using the Restrict access action for Fabric, no additional action is required.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Semantic-model DLP evaluation is skipped when service principal authentication initiates publishing, republishing or refresh.
claims.quote: DLP evaluation of the semantic model doesn't occur if either of the following is true: An account using service principal authentication initiates the event (publish, republish, on-demand refresh, scheduled refresh).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Semantic-model DLP evaluation is skipped when the model owner is a service principal.
claims.quote: DLP evaluation of the semantic model doesn't occur if either of the following is true: ... The semantic model owner is a service principal.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Fabric DLP does not support semantic models using DirectQuery or live connections.
claims.quote: DLP policies for Fabric aren't supported for sample semantic models, streaming datasets, or semantic models that connect to their data source via DirectQuery or live connection.

claims.claim: Fabric DLP applies only to data in tables stored in Delta format.
claims.quote: DLP policies for Fabric apply only on data in tables stored in Delta format.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Advanced classifiers such as exact data match and trainable classifiers are unsupported and return no matches.
claims.quote: Advanced classifiers, such as exact data match (EDM), trainable classifiers, credential classifiers, and named entities aren't supported by DLP for Fabric.

claims.claim: Other classifiers in a policy containing an unsupported advanced classifier can still return results.
claims.quote: Other classifiers specified in the policy return results if any.

claims.claim: Semantic models are evaluated on publish, republish, on-demand refresh and scheduled refresh.
claims.quote: DLP policies evaluate a semantic model whenever one of the following events occurs: Publish; Republish; On-demand refresh; Scheduled refresh

claims.claim: Lakehouses and other Fabric items are evaluated when their data changes.
claims.quote: DLP policies evaluate a Fabric item, such as a lakehouse, SQL database, or Mirrored database, when the data within it changes.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance controls
claims.claim: Enabling restrict access automatically allows user overrides.
claims.quote: When you enable the restrict access action, user overrides are automatically allowed.

claims.claim: Item owners may override restrictions depending on the configured override options.
claims.quote: owners - that is, users with an Admin or Member role in the workspace where the item is located ... The selection of response options they have depends on the choices you make in the User overrides section.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: DLP actions are supported only in workspaces hosted on Fabric or Premium capacities.
claims.quote: DLP actions are supported only for workspaces hosted in Fabric or Premium capacities.

claims.claim: Onboarding a new tenant to DLP can take a few hours.
claims.quote: Onboarding a new tenant to DLP can take a few hours, depending on the number of supported workspaces that are being onboarded.

claims.claim: Policy creators must belong to one of the five listed compliance, information protection or security role groups.
claims.quote: The account you use to create DLP policies must be a member of one of these role groups: Compliance administrator; Compliance data administrator; Information Protection; Information Protection Admin; Security administrator

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The configuration page requires the admin account to have Microsoft 365 E5, E5 Compliance, E5 Information Protection & Governance or Purview capacities.
claims.quote: The admin account that sets up the DLP rules must be assigned one of the following licenses: Microsoft 365 E5; Microsoft 365 E5 Compliance; Microsoft 365 E5 Information Protection & Governance; Purview capacities

claims.claim: The Fabric DLP configuration page names no licence for users whose access is restricted.
claims.quote: Searched: Fabric DLP restricted users license requirements configure admin account. Opened fabric/governance/data-loss-prevention-configure, including its complete SKU/subscriptions licensing section; it lists only admin-account licences.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: DLP evaluation workloads affect capacity consumption and the overview points to the Purview billing models page.
claims.quote: DLP evaluation workloads impact capacity consumption. For information about how this consumption is metered and billed, see Learn about Microsoft Purview billing models.

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, combining documented admin licensing with consumption billing.
claims.quote: The pay-as-you-go billing model builds on the per-user licensing model. The two are complementary, not mutually exclusive.

claims.claim: Variable cost is supported by a daily asset-based consumption meter.
claims.quote: You're charged for each day that a policy covers an asset.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Purview pay-as-you-go covers Microsoft Fabric and uses Azure-based consumption billing.
claims.quote: The billing mechanisms are Azure based, so you must associate your Microsoft 365 tenant with an active Azure subscription.

claims.claim: Fabric DLP assets are charged for each day they are covered by a policy.
claims.quote: You're charged for each day that a policy covers an asset. ... | Azure | Fabric | Supported item types | Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention |

claims.claim: An asset counts when its location is in policy scope even if it does not match the policy conditions.
claims.quote: The asset doesn't have to match a policy's conditions to be counted, it just has to be in a location that's in the scope of a policy.

claims.claim: Microsoft's example counts 250 assets when a DLP policy covers five of ten workspaces holding 50 assets each.
claims.quote: A tenant has 10 Fabric workspaces, each with 50 assets. The policy only applies to five of these Fabric workspaces. The asset count for this policy is 250.

claims.claim: The cited Fabric DLP and billing models pages quote no Fabric DLP rate.
claims.quote: Searched: Fabric DLP restrict access pricing separate charge asset price; Fabric DLP price asset. Read the Fabric DLP overview, configuration page and purview/purview-billing-models: they give requirements, units and an asset example, but no Fabric DLP rate.

claims.claim: A separate charge specifically for the restrict access action beyond policy asset counting is not published in the documentation found.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Purview Fabric DLP restrict access separate action charge pricing rate per asset; site:learn.microsoft.com/purview Fabric restrict access billing. Read Fabric DLP overview/configuration and Purview billing models; no separate action charge found.

claims.claim: Excluding workspaces changes which assets the policy covers.
claims.quote: Assets are counted based on the number of items that are in the scope of a policy. ... The policy only applies to five of these Fabric workspaces. The asset count for this policy is 250.

claims.claim: The roadmap does not list US Government clouds.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: DLP for Fabric is unsupported in China North.
claims.quote: DLP policies for Fabric aren't supported in the China North region.

claims.claim: The overview lists semantic models, lakehouses, warehouses, KQL databases, mirrored databases, SQL databases and Cosmos databases as supported item types.
claims.quote: DLP policies for Fabric and Power BI currently support the following item types. Semantic models; Lakehouses; Warehouses; KQL databases; Mirrored databases; SQL databases; Cosmos databases

claims.claim: Fabric DLP policies apply to workspaces.
claims.quote: DLP policies apply to workspaces. Only workspaces hosted in Fabric or Premium capacities are supported.

claims.claim: Sample semantic models are unsupported.
claims.quote: DLP policies for Fabric aren't supported for sample semantic models

claims.claim: Streaming datasets are unsupported.
claims.quote: DLP policies for Fabric aren't supported for sample semantic models, streaming datasets

claims.claim: Fabric DLP requires the Custom category and Custom policy rather than other templates.
claims.quote: Choose the Custom category and then the Custom policy template. ... No other categories or templates are currently supported.

claims.claim: Admin units are not supported for DLP in Fabric and Power BI.
claims.quote: Select Next when you get to the Assign admin units page. Admin units are not supported for DLP in Fabric and Power BI.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: New-DlpComplianceRule with Name, Policy, ContentContainsSensitiveInformation and BlockAccess $true creates a sensitive-information rule that blocks access.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls: second table row

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: second table row
claims.claim: New-DlpCompliancePolicy -PowerBIDlpLocation All -PowerBIDlpLocationException <workspaceID> -Mode Enable creates an enabled policy excluding the specified workspace.

claims.fix: Append to both copies of the workspace-scope row's note: 'The PowerShell reference limits -PowerBIDlpLocation and -PowerBIDlpLocationException to workspaces hosted in Premium Gen2 capacities; the Fabric configuration page instead says Fabric or Premium capacities.' Retain the existing call and test-tenant caveat.

claims.where: controls[0].note; controls[1].note; Governance controls: table notes
claims.claim: After choosing Custom policy, admins name and describe the policy and continue through Assign admin units without assigning units.
claims.quote: Name the policy and provide a meaningful description. When done, select Next. ... Select Next when you get to the Assign admin units page.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: Within the restrict access section, admins select the Block users option and choose everyone or outsiders only.
claims.quote: select Block users from receiving email, or accessing shared SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams files, and Power BI items. Then choose whether to block everyone or only people outside your organization.

claims.claim: Restrict access is a rule action, while the policy's location settings determine workspace coverage.
claims.quote: Select Fabric and Power BI workspaces as the location for the DLP policy. ... On the Customize advanced DLP rules page ... Select Create rule.

claims.where: Governance controls: paragraph after table; Open questions
claims.claim: The two cmdlet reference pages document general DLP operations without naming Fabric lakehouses or semantic models.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Fabric DLP restrict access PowerShell BlockAccess PowerBIDlpLocation. Opened both New-DlpComplianceRule and New-DlpCompliancePolicy references; searched their full text for Fabric, lakehouse and semantic model, with no matches.

claims.claim: The rule's User overrides section sets the available override options.
claims.quote: The selection of response options they have depends on the choices you make in the User overrides section.

claims.claim: Admins can monitor Fabric DLP alerts on the Alerts page in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: If you enable alerts in the policy, an alert records on the data loss prevention Alerts page in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Fabric and Power BI DLP data can be viewed in Activity explorer.
claims.quote: You can view data from DLP for Fabric and Power BI in Activity explorer.

claims.claim: The Learn overview does not state whether its semantic-model service-principal evaluation exception also applies to lakehouses.
claims.quote: Searched: Fabric lakehouse DLP service principal evaluation skipped; lakehouses DLP service principal. Read the overview's Semantic models and Fabric Items sections and troubleshooting page; the exception is stated only for semantic models, not lakehouses.

claims.claim: Configured actions run automatically on a policy match, so an ordinary refresh can trigger restriction without individual approval.
claims.quote: When DLP policies evaluate a supported item type, they check if it matches the conditions in a DLP policy. If it does, the policy's specified actions take place.
